catalog_description: License audit and true-up records comparing entitled to installed counts, with the resulting gap, true-up cost, and supporting evidence.
Active issued licenses or permits, with holder, type, issue and expiration dates, conditions, jurisdiction, and current status.
Renewal applications for existing licenses, tracking submission, updated requirements, fees, condition changes, and outcome.
Qualifying life events such as marriage, birth, adoption, or coverage loss that open a mid-year benefits enrollment window.
Limited partners in a fund, with their commitment, contributions to date, and governance rights for compliance tracking.
Individual head of livestock, with identity, breed, sex, birth or acquisition date, status, parentage, and the mob it belongs to.
Identifiers attached to an animal, such as RFID ear tags or scheme device numbers, and the traceability registration they carry.
Managed groups of animals handled collectively for movements, treatments, and pasture allocation.
Borrower requests to originate a loan, with amount, purpose, loan type, term, collateral, and lifecycle from draft to funded.
Releases of approved loan funds, with date, amount, tranching, destination account, and conditions satisfied.
Physical or organizational locations referenced across the system, used to place and group other records.
Application log stream entries, structured and unstructured, indexed for search and correlated with metrics and traces for root-cause analysis.
First-notice-of-loss events giving rise to a claim, with occurrence date, location, cause, loss type, and description.
Customers enrolled in the loyalty program, with tier, accrued points balance, enrollment date, and opt-in status.
Tier definitions in the loyalty program, with qualifying thresholds, benefits, and retention rules that members are assigned to.
Point-earning and point-spending events for loyalty members: purchases, bonuses, redemptions, expiries, and adjustments.
Active capital commitments from a limited partner to a fund, tracking committed, called, and distributed amounts plus current value.
Know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering results for a limited partner, including sanction screening, captured at subscription and re-screened periodically.
Prospective limited partners being fundraised, tracking the relationship before any capital commitment is closed.
Quarterly performance reports for limited partners per fund, with position marks, fund metrics, and general-partner commentary.
Subscription documents collected during limited-partner onboarding: the legal commitment, KYC and AML results, and accreditation attestation.
External Learning Record Store endpoints that xAPI learning statements are routed to.
Per-job equipment telemetry logged from machinery, covering operating parameters, application rates, GPS track, and alarms.
Defect and non-conformance records captured from inspections or driver reports before a work order is raised.
Reminders sent to a manager when one of their direct reports has overdue or upcoming training.
Manufacturing bills of materials restructured for assembly order, with phantom-part rollups, kitting, and process-specific decompositions.
Routings defining the ordered sequence of operations to produce a part, with work center, setup time, run time, and resource allocations.
Mooring balls in a mooring field, with position, tackle, weight rating, and the assigned vessel.
Wet berths at a dock, with number, length, beam and draft limits, utilities, and service status.
Defined slices of the market by industry, size, geography, or motion that a plan targets.
Competitive, pricing, and churn-risk signals aggregated across many conversations, summarizing what the market is saying overall.
Top-down assignments of budget from a marketing budget to a plan line, campaign, or channel, routed through approval and reconciled against spend.
Pools of marketing funds for a period, unit, or region that are approved and then allocated top-down across plans, campaigns, and channels.
Shared campaign and content calendars laying marketing activity out across time, teams, and channels for visibility and coordination.
Marketing campaign definitions across email, multi-channel, and account-based plays, with target audience, schedule, content variants, and KPIs.
Email templates and sent instances at marketing scale, with open, click, bounce, and unsubscribe metrics and deliverability state.
Lead-capture form definitions, with fields, mapping to leads and contacts, conditional logic, and post-submit routing.
Plan-level performance and marketing-ROI measures such as results, pipeline contribution, and return, computed against the plans and budgets that funded the activity.
Lines within a marketing plan, each a planned activity or program with objective, owner, time window, and allocated budget.
Annual or quarterly marketing plans, the top-level container organizing objectives, plan lines, and budget, approved before execution.
Committed or actual marketing expenditures attributed to a budget allocation and plan line, reconciled to compute remaining budget and variance.
Audit records of a matching or scoring batch, capturing model version, inputs, outputs such as fit scores and recommendations, and timestamp.
Decision logic identifying candidate duplicate records within or across sources, with field weights and threshold scores.
Recorded meal and rest-break events evidencing compliance with labor-law break requirements, with waiver attestation where applicable.
Per-campaign media-buying plans broken down by outlet, channel, daypart, audience, flight dates, and budget allocation.
Medical equipment in clinical use such as infusion pumps, ventilators, and imaging systems, as a specialized regulated asset class.
Matched mentor and mentee relationships, with goals, meeting cadence, and status.
Survivorship rules defining which source system's value wins per field when two records merge.
Periodic compensation review cycles, with budget pool, eligibility, calibration step, approval chain, and effective date.
Per-employee proposed merit increases, bonuses, and equity refreshes for a cycle, with calibration adjustments and final approval.
Positioning and messaging frameworks for a product or segment, with pillars, proof points, and approved copy.
Periodic reads of a utility meter, manual or wireless, that become a billable utility line.
Operator-collected or automated consumption readings, with read date, consumption value, unit, read method, and anomaly flags.
Row-level and metric-level access policies at the semantic-definition tier, governing which business unit sees which metric.
Canonical, certified definitions of a business metric: numerator, denominator, filters, dimensions, time grain, ownership, and lineage to sources.
Cached or pre-aggregated metric rollups served from columnar storage by the semantic layer.
Time-series metric streams from instrumented applications: counters, gauges, histograms, and summaries tied to release versions.
Bulk-tank or per-cow milk-quality results, covering cell count, bacterial count, butterfat, protein, and antibiotic-residue screening.
Per-cow milking events from parlor or robotic systems, with milk yield, conductivity, and duration.
Training metadata for machine-learning models, covering feature set, training window, version, accuracy, and retraining schedule.
Registered machine-learning models with versions, training-data lineage, evaluation metrics, deployment endpoints, and approval state.
Recorded movements of a mob between paddocks, properties, or external destinations, with date, head count, origin, destination, and reason.
App distribution units for mobile deployment, with app identifier, version, manifest, store link, and silent-install flag.
AI-generated next-move suggestions for an employee, with rationale and freshness.
Observed insider activity events captured from endpoint, email, file, cloud, identity, or removable-media telemetry, evaluated by detection rules.
Filtered, human-relevant events that crossed a threshold or matched a pattern, enriched with priority and routing, ready to be paged or ticketed.
Raw events from monitored systems: state changes, threshold crossings, status updates, and log signals consumed for correlation.
Monitoring policies defining what to monitor, at what frequency and thresholds, for which configuration items, often auto-bound by class.
A managed service provider's end-customer organizations, with site hierarchy, contacts, contract portfolio, and asset estate.
Service contracts between a managed service provider and an end-customer, covering block-hour, retainer, per-device, or managed-service models, consumption, renewal, and SLA terms.
Invoices issued by a managed service provider to its end-customer, combining recurring subscription lines, out-of-contract billable work, and tax.
Billable service tickets against a managed service provider's contract, with time-tracked work, billable category, SLA timer, and dispatch state.
Technician time entries per ticket, contract, or customer, with category tagging, billable classification, approval, and feeds to payroll and billing.
Third-party store quality assessments covering customer experience, compliance, and staff courtesy, distinct from internal store audits.
Government-issued identity numbers for a worker, such as social security or national insurance numbers, held with restricted access and validity dates.
Negotiation rules and fallback positions guiding how clauses may be redlined and which concessions are pre-approved.
Historical baseline performance profiles per path, flow, or link, covering median and p95 latency, loss, and jitter, used for anomaly detection.
Captured packet and session flows, with source and destination addresses, ports, protocols, bytes transferred, and duration.
Physical or virtual network interfaces on monitored devices, serving as the collection point for traffic flow capture.
Telco network inventory of ports, circuits, IP address blocks, fiber routes, and access-node ports, with allocated or free status.
Path traces from source to destination, with the ordered hop sequence, per-hop latency, cumulative loss, and round-trip time.
Threshold breaches or anomalies on network performance metrics, with severity, affected path or flow, and baseline correlation.
Time-series of latency, jitter, packet loss, and throughput sampled across flows, links, and application paths for network SLO reporting.
Periodic captures of network connectivity: device adjacency, link status, and interface roles, used for visualization and root-cause correlation.
Placements of a worker on a performance-by-potential nine-box grid per cycle, feeding succession planning and high-potential identification.
Record-triggered workflows, scheduled jobs, or external API calls defined in a no-code platform.
User-defined containers for a no-code deployment: a self-contained namespace for tables, views, automations, and access.
Public or authenticated intake forms authored in a no-code database.
User-defined schema inside a no-code base: tables, fields with types, linked-record relationships, formulas, and views.
Switchable presentation layers such as grid, gallery, kanban, calendar, or timeline over a no-code base.
Reusable email, in-app, and chat templates with merge fields, used by automation rules and manager reminders.
Multi-touch outbound nurture flows, with branching paths, wait conditions, exit criteria, and content trees.
A learner's scored result against an observation checklist, with observer signoff.
On-the-job competency checklists that an observer scores against for field-skill assessment.
Real-time or snapshot occupancy state for a space: desk booked, room reserved, or actual check-in via badge or mobile.
Medical surveillance and exposure records such as respirator fit tests, audiometric tests, or fitness-for-duty evaluations, retained per occupational-health rules.
Immutable, append-only audit logs of every applicant-flow event for federal contractors, carrying the actor, timestamp, and compliance-relevant fields.
Approval steps in the offer-approval chain, triggered when an offer exceeds band, includes non-standard equity, or matches other escalation rules.
